studies.description: M. marinum is a fish pathogen that usually only infects human skin, but it is genetically related to Mycobacterium tuberculosis and Mycobacterium avium and has similar pathogenic mechanisms to these human pathogens. M. marinum and M. avium have been found in biofilms in water distribution systems and showerheads. Therefore, M. marinum is a biosafety level 2 model organism for biofilm-forming pathogenic mycobacteria. M. marinum prefer to form biofilms on hydrophobic surfaces and hydrophobic materials are used on the ISS, an example is silicone. In this study we wanted to examine the transcriptome changes of M. marinum exposed to simulated microgravity in biofilm-promoting medium. M. marinum expressing red fluorescent protein were grown in biofilm-promoting medium in flaskettes containing a piece of PDMS membrane attached to the slide. After filling the flaskettes, cultures were shipped to Kennedy Space station overnight. The flaskettes were attached to the RPM 2.0, or a lab-designed 3D clinostat which were positioned in the same incubator. For the normal gravity control, the flaskette was positioned on the shelf next to the microgravity simulators. After 4 days at 31 degrees C, the bacteria in suspension were used to prepare RNA and RNA-seq was performed to examine gene expression changes.

protocols.description: Red fluorescent protein (RFP)-expressing M. marinum at OD600 ~0.2 in biofilm-promoting medium (7H9 Middlebrook, 0.5% glycerol, 100 ug/ mL cycloheximide) were sealed without bubbles in a flaskette. The flaskettes were shipped to Kennedy Space Center overnight. The flaskettes were attached to the RPM 2.0 or a lab-developed 3D clinostat. The two devices were positioned in the same humidified incubator at 31 degrees Celsius. Sealed flaskettes were also positioned on the shelf near the devices and these were the normal gravity controls. Three independent cultures were used to generate three independent samples. One sample for each of the 3D clinostat and for the normal gravity were set-up the same way, including overnight incubation at room temperature, but the samples were incubated on the 3D clinostat or at normal gravity at 31 degrees Celsius at LSU Health Sciences Center. All flaskettes were incubated for 4 days at 31 degree Celsius before sample collection. The 3D clinostat was operated with inner frame at 1.5 rpm and outer frame operated at 3.875 rpm. The RPM 2.0 was operated in partial gravity mode using the 0g file to simulate microgravity.
protocols.name: treatment protocol

protocols.description: Bacteria in suspension were subjected to centrifugation for 5 minutes at 2000 g. The pellet was resuspended in 1 mL Trizol and and put in a tube with Lysing Matrix B beads.
protocols.name: sample collection

protocols.description: The lysing matrix beads were subjected to 3 times 30 second cycles in an Omni Bead ruptor at speed 6.45. They were cooled on ice between the cycles. After removing the solution from the beads, a chloroform/isoamyl extraction was performed and the RNA precipitated overnight at 4C. The RNA pellet was washed with 75% ethanol, resuspended in 100 ul nuclease-free water and frozen at -80C. Samples were transported to LSUHSC on dry ice. The RNA was further purified using the Qiagen RNeasy Kit with a 45 minute on-column DNase digestion. RNA was quantitated with a Qubit RNA assay (ThermoFisher Scientific, MA) and RNA quality was determined with the Agilent TapeStation RNA assay (Agilent Technologies, CA). RIN was equal or greater than 7.4 for the samples.
protocols.name: Nucleic Acid Extraction

protocols.description: Libraries were prepared from 1 ug RNA from each sample with the Stranded Total RNA Prep, Ligation with Ribo-Zero Plus kit (Illumina, CA). The average library size was determined using an Agilent TapeStation D1000 assay (Agilent Technologies) and libraries were quantitated with qPCR (Bio-rad CFX96 Touch Real-Time PCR, NEB Library Quant Kit for Illumina).
protocols.name: Library Construction

protocols.description: Libraries were normalized to 1 nM and pooled. The library pool was denatured and diluted to approximately 1.5pM. A PhiX library was spiked in as an internal control. Paired-end 99 x 49 base pair sequencing was performed on an Illumina NextSeq 550 and samples had 28-32 million pair-end reads.
protocols.name: Nucleic Acid Sequencing

protocols.description: Quality assessment of reads was performed with FastQC v0.11.9 and reports were combined with MultiQC v1.12. rRNA percentages of reads were estimated with the 'hts_SeqScreener' program of htstream v1.3.3 screened against a fasta file of Mycobacterium rRNA sequences retrieved from NCBI on 20-Oct-2022.
